prerequisiteEdges.justification: The product, quotient and power rules are derived by counting repeated factors, which requires reading exponent notation as repeated multiplication.
The identity a^0=1 is obtained by applying the quotient-of-powers rule to a^n/a^n, so that rule must already be available.
Prime-factor tests on denominators and place-value remainders use integer division and remainders the learner must already compute reliably.
Learners first need a working distinction between terminating, recurring and non-repeating expansions before they can treat √n and π as a different class.
Switching among power, decimal and radical forms in scale-factor calculations uses the full set of exponent laws including the zero case.
Choosing an appropriate representation for a hypotenuse or circumference requires already knowing that the exact value is irrational and only approximately decimal.

misconceptions.label: Sign error on subtraction
misconceptions.description: Replaces a−(−b) with a−b or treats −a−b as −(a−b) when simplifying integer expressions.

misconceptions.label: Treats exponent as multiplier
misconceptions.description: Computes 2^3 as 2×3=6 instead of three factors of 2.

misconceptions.label: Adds exponents on different bases
misconceptions.description: Writes 2^3×5^2 as 10^5 (or 2^5) by adding exponents even though the bases differ.

misconceptions.label: Multiplies exponents on a product
misconceptions.description: Replaces (2×3)^4 with 2^4×3 or with 2×3^4 instead of 2^4×3^4.

misconceptions.label: Zero power equals zero
misconceptions.description: States that any non-zero a^0 equals 0 rather than 1.

misconceptions.label: Treats recurring as irrational
misconceptions.description: Classifies 0.333… or 1/3 as irrational because the decimal does not terminate.

misconceptions.label: Treats π as exactly 22/7
misconceptions.description: Replaces π with 22/7 in every calculation and treats the fraction as the exact value.

items.stem: Simplify 3^4 × 3^2 using a single power of 3.

options.rationale: Multiplies the exponents instead of adding them for a product of powers.
Treats the product as if the bases were different and combines them incorrectly.

items.keyRationale: For identical bases, the product-of-powers law gives 3^{4+2} = 3^6.

options.rationale: A non-zero number to the power zero equals 1, as shown by 5^n ÷ 5^n = 5^0 = 1.
Treats any number to the power zero as zero.
Leaves the base unchanged instead of applying the zero-exponent result.

items.keyRationale: Equal powers in a quotient cancel to give a^0 = 1 for a ≠ 0.

items.stem: Does the decimal for 7/20 terminate or recur?

options.text: It recurs and is therefore irrational.
options.rationale: Treats a non-terminating look as irrational even though 7/20 is rational and actually terminates.
Misreads the prime factors of 20 and expects a repeating block.

items.keyRationale: A fraction in lowest terms terminates iff the denominator’s primes are only 2 and/or 5.

items.stem: Between which two neighbouring tenths does √2 lie on a number line?

options.rationale: Confuses √2 with π and treats 22/7 as an exact location.

options.text: It cannot be placed because recurring decimals are irrational.
options.rationale: Mixes recurring rationals with irrationals and refuses to locate √2.

items.keyRationale: Square both neighbouring tenths to sandwich 2 and hence locate √2.

items.stem: A square tile has side length 2^3 cm. What is its area in square centimetres, written as a single ordinary number?

options.rationale: Replaces the length with π ≈ 22/7 instead of evaluating the power.
